title: Präteritum (The Simple Past)
description: Learn how to use the formal written past tense for all verbs, not just the modal verbs.

examples.german: Gestern las ich ein Buch.
examples.english: Yesterday I read a book.

examples.german: Er kaufte ein neues Auto.
examples.english: He bought a new car.

conjugationTable: Regular (kaufen): kaufte, kauftest, kaufte, kauften, kauftet, kauften
Irregular (lesen): las, lasest, las, lasen, last, lasen
errorTraps: In the Präteritum, the 'ich' and 'er/sie/es' forms are ALWAYS identical!

title: Plusquamperfekt (The Past Perfect)
description: How to talk about an event that happened before another event in the past (the 'past of the past').

examples.german: Nachdem ich gegessen hatte, ging ich schlafen.
examples.english: After I had eaten, I went to sleep.

errorTraps: The Plusquamperfekt is almost never used alone. It is used to show sequence (Event A happened before Event B).

title: Passiv (The Passive Voice)
description: Focus on the action itself, rather than who is doing it. (e.g. 'The house is being built').

examples.german: Das Auto wird repariert.
examples.english: The car is being repaired.

examples.german: Das Haus wurde 1990 gebaut.
examples.english: The house was built in 1990.

conjugationTable: werden: werde, wirst, wird, werden, werdet, werden
wurden: wurde, wurdest, wurde, wurden, wurdet, wurden
errorTraps: Do not confuse Passive 'werden' with Future tense 'werden'. Future uses the infinitive at the end, Passive uses the Past Participle!

title: Relative Clauses and Pronouns
description: How to combine two sentences by referring back to a noun using 'who', 'which', or 'that'.

examples.german: Das ist der Mann, der hier wohnt.
examples.english: That is the man who lives here.

examples.german: Das Buch, das ich lese, ist gut.
examples.english: The book that I am reading is good.

conjugationTable: Nom Relative: der, die, das, die
Acc Relative: den, die, das, die
Relative clauses are dependent clauses (verb goes to the end!).
errorTraps: The relative pronoun gets its GENDER from the noun it refers to, but its CASE from its job in the new clause.

title: Relative Pronouns in the Dative Case
description: Using relative pronouns for indirect objects or after dative prepositions.

examples.german: Der Mann, dem ich helfe, ist alt.
examples.english: The man whom I am helping is old.

examples.german: Die Frau, mit der ich spreche, ist nett.
examples.english: The woman with whom I am speaking is nice.

errorTraps: In the plural dative, the relative pronoun is NOT 'den', it is 'denen'!

title: N-Declension (Weak Nouns)
description: A special group of masculine nouns that add an '-n' or '-en' ending in every case except the Nominative.

examples.german: Der Junge spielt (Nom). Ich sehe den Jungen (Acc).
examples.english: The boy plays. I see the boy.

conjugationTable: Nom: der Student | Acc: den Studenten | Dat: dem Studenten
Nom: der Name | Acc: den Namen | Dat: dem Namen
errorTraps: Do not confuse these endings with plural endings! 'den Studenten' can mean 'the student' (singular accusative) OR 'the students' (plural accusative).

title: Genitive Case (The 4th Case)
description: The case of possession. Equivalent to 'of the' or the English apostrophe 's'.

examples.german: Das ist das Auto des Vaters.
examples.english: That is the father's car (the car of the father).

examples.german: Die Farbe der Blume ist rot.
examples.english: The color of the flower is red.

errorTraps: For masculine and neuter nouns, you MUST add an '-s' or '-es' to the end of the noun itself! (des Mannes, des Autos).

title: Genitive Prepositions
description: Prepositions that force the following noun into the Genitive case.

examples.german: Wegen des Regens bleibe ich zu Hause.
examples.english: Because of the rain, I stay home.

examples.german: Während des Films bin ich eingeschlafen.
examples.english: During the film, I fell asleep.

errorTraps: In spoken German, many native speakers incorrectly use the Dative case with 'wegen' (wegen dem Regen). However, in written B1 German, you MUST use the Genitive (wegen des Regens)!

title: Infinitive Clauses with 'zu'
description: How to combine sentences using 'to' + infinitive (e.g. I have no time TO sleep).

examples.german: Ich habe keine Zeit, das Buch zu lesen.
examples.english: I have no time to read the book.

examples.german: Er lernt Deutsch, um in Berlin zu leben.
examples.english: He learns German in order to live in Berlin.

conjugationTable: Separable verbs: aufzumachen, einzukaufen (zu goes in the middle!)
errorTraps: You cannot use an infinitive clause if the subject changes! 'I hope that HE comes' must use a 'dass' clause. 'I hope TO come' can use a 'zu' clause.

title: Konjunktiv II for Unreal Conditions
description: Using 'would', 'could', and 'had' to talk about hypothetical, unreal situations (If I had a million dollars...).

examples.german: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich dir helfen.
examples.english: If I had time, I would help you.

errorTraps: Do not use 'würde haben' or 'würde sein'. Native speakers always use 'hätte' and 'wäre'.

title: Two-Part Conjunctions
description: Conjunctions that come in pairs (e.g. either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also).

examples.german: Er spricht nicht nur Englisch, sondern auch Deutsch.
examples.english: He speaks not only English, but also German.

examples.german: Ich trinke weder Kaffee noch Tee.
examples.english: I drink neither coffee nor tea.

conjugationTable: sowohl ... als auch (both ... and / as well as)
nicht nur ... sondern auch (not only ... but also)
errorTraps: 'weder...noch' already contains a negative meaning. Do not add 'nicht' to the sentence!

title: Adjective Declension without Article
description: How to decline adjectives when there is absolutely no article (der/ein) before the noun.

examples.german: Wir trinken kalten Kaffee.
examples.english: We drink cold coffee.

examples.german: Mit großer Freude präsentiere ich...
examples.english: With great joy I present...

conjugationTable: When there is no article, the adjective must take over the 'signal ending' of the definite article.
errorTraps: Genitive Masculine and Neuter is the weird exception! Instead of taking an -es (kaltes Wassers), it takes an -en (kalten Wassers) because the noun already has the -s.

title: Da-words and Wo-words
description: How to refer to abstract things or objects without repeating the preposition + noun (e.g. 'about it', 'for it').

examples.german: Ich freue mich darauf.
examples.english: I am looking forward to it.

examples.german: Worauf wartest du?
examples.english: What are you waiting for?

conjugationTable: da + preposition = about it, for it, with it
wo + preposition = what about, what for, with what
If the preposition starts with a vowel, add an 'r' (daRauf, woRüber)
errorTraps: Da-words and Wo-words can ONLY be used for things, objects, or concepts! You cannot use them for people (You cannot say 'Ich warte darauf' to mean 'I wait for him').

title: Verbs with Fixed Prepositions (Advanced)
description: Expanding your vocabulary of verbs that demand specific prepositions.

examples.german: Es hängt vom Wetter ab.
examples.english: It depends on the weather.

examples.german: Ich kümmere mich um den Hund.
examples.english: I take care of the dog.

conjugationTable: sich kümmern um (Acc) - to take care of
sich beschweren über (Acc) - to complain about
errorTraps: Notice how 'an' takes Accusative for 'erinnern an', but Dative for 'teilnehmen an'. Fixed preposition verbs must be memorized with their specific case!

title: Adjective + Preposition Combinations
description: Just like verbs, some adjectives are permanently glued to specific prepositions.

examples.german: Ich bin stolz auf dich.
examples.english: I am proud of you.

examples.german: Er ist interessiert an Kunst.
examples.english: He is interested in art.

conjugationTable: verliebt in (+ Acc) - in love with
errorTraps: Do not translate literally! 'Proud OF' uses 'auf' (on), not 'von' (of).
